quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If another driver is following you too closely, what should you do?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to deal with a tailgater is to get them in front of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may only make the driver tailgate you faster.

questions.question: What is true about the front brake?

options.text: Use it only when you need to stop quickly.
Use it only on slippery roads.
It is not as strong as the rear brake.
It is safe to use if you use it correctly.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is safe to use if you use it correctly.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes any time you slow down or stop. The front brake is stronger than the rear brake. It is safe to use as long as you use it properly.

questions.question: How much stopping power does the front brake provide on a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: About three-quarters
questions.explanation: The front brake on a motorcycle is stronger than the rear brake. It provides about three-fourths of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: The center of a lane usually has an oily strip. When is this area safe for motorcycles?

options.text: Usually, unless the road is wet

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually, unless the road is wet
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in a strip down the center of the lane. This area is generally safe for motorcycles unless the road is wet. The strip is usually narrow enough that you can ride around it while still staying in the center part of the lane.

questions.question: If you carry a load in a sidecar, how does this affect stopping distance?

options.text: It stays the same as a two-wheel motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may increase.
questions.explanation: Adding a load makes the motorcycle heavier, which increases how hard it is to stop. This means the stopping distance may get longer. Start slowing down earlier when carrying a load or passenger in a sidecar.

questions.question: Which protects your eyes from the wind?
questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect your eyes from wind. Windshields, eyeglasses, and sunglasses do not provide enough eye protection.

questions.question: When riding in curves, turning, or entering a highway, which group formation is best?
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is usually best for group riding. However, use a single-file line when going through curves, making turns, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, it should have all these features except:

options.text: Meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards

questions.correctAnswerText: Looks attractive
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around and have no defects like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.correctAnswerText: Day and night
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright colors and reflective materials all the time to help other drivers see you better.

questions.question: What is the best way to choose a lane position?

options.text: Pick one position and always use it.
Change positions often to stay alert.
Choose the position that gives you the most space around you.
Never use the center lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Choose the position that gives you the most space around you.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change all the time, so the safest lane position also changes. Choose the position that gives you the most space cushion and makes it easiest for other drivers to see you.

questions.question: Motorcycles must have all of the following, except:

options.text: A white light for the license plate.
At least one red brake light.
A blue reflector on the rear.

questions.correctAnswerText: A blue reflector on the rear.
questions.explanation: In Oregon, motorcycles must have: one to three white headlights; at least one red taillight; one white license plate light; at least one red brake light; amber turn signal lights (for motorcycles made after 1972); a red reflector on the rear; at least one rearview mirror; a horn; fenders on all wheels; at least one brake; and a working exhaust system. All lights must meet U.S. Department of Transportation standards.

questions.question: After entering a turn, you should roll on the throttle and:

options.text: Keep a steady speed or speed up slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a steady speed or speed up slowly.
questions.explanation: Roll on the throttle through a turn to keep your suspension stable. Keep your speed steady or speed up slowly as you go through the turn.

questions.question: Which of the following protects a rider the best?
questions.correctAnswerText: A face shield
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield that does not shatter protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles protect your eyes only, not your whole face. A windshield or eyeglasses do not provide the same protection as goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: To reduce your risk of a crash, you should:

options.text: Use your turn signals when you plan to change lanes.
Look only 15 feet ahead of your motorcycle.
Not use your headlight during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals when you plan to change lanes.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, you should be visible to others, signal your intentions, keep safe distance from other vehicles, look at least 12 seconds ahead, spot and avoid hazards, and be ready for changing road conditions.

questions.question: You should increase your following distance:

options.text: When there are only a few vehicles on the road.
When drivers are following the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the road is slippery.
questions.explanation: You need more space if your motorcycle takes longer to stop. Increase your following distance when the road is slippery, when you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or when traffic is heavy and another driver may cut in front of you.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, you should:

options.text: Position yourself so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
Ride on the far left side of the lane.
Ride on the far right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position yourself so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When riding behind a car, position yourself so the other driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Riding in the center of the lane usually puts you in the middle of their mirror, where they are most likely to notice you.

questions.question: To work well, an eye or face shield should have all of the following, except:

options.text: Be too tight to wear sunglasses or eyeglasses.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be too tight to wear sunglasses or eyeglasses.
questions.explanation: An effective eye or face shield must have no scratches, resist breaking, give clear side vision, fasten securely, allow air to pass through to prevent fogging, and have room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: You may pass in a no passing zone.
You may go up to 10 mph over the speed limit to complete the pass.
You must start and finish the pass in a legal passing zone.
You must pass on the shoulder if one is available.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must start and finish the pass in a legal passing zone.
questions.explanation: Passing must be done within the posted speed limit and only where it is safe and legal.

questions.question: When riding downhill on a motorcycle with a sidecar:

options.text: Stopping is easier than on a motorcycle without a sidecar.
Stopping takes longer than on a motorcycle without a sidecar.
Stopping is about the same as on a motorcycle without a sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping takes longer than on a motorcycle without a sidecar.
questions.explanation: A sidecar adds weight to the motorcycle, which means you need more braking power to stop. Slowing down and stopping take longer when riding downhill compared to riding on a flat surface.

questions.question: A three-wheeled motorcycle:

options.text: Handles turns about the same as a two-wheeled motorcycle.
Handles turns differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
Should not be used on curves.
Should use the shoulder when taking a curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Handles turns differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
questions.explanation: A three-wheeled motorcycle or a motorcycle with a sidecar turns differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.

questions.question: How can a motorcyclist prevent other vehicles from sharing their lane?

options.text: Ride on the left side of the lane.
Ride in the center of the lane.
Give dirty looks to other drivers.
Ride in a zigzag pattern to fill the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to stop other drivers from trying to squeeze in next to you.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks can affect a rider's ability to ride?
questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Even one alcoholic drink can affect your ability to ride. Riding while under the influence of alcohol is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help you avoid serious injury in a crash?
questions.correctAnswerText: Have a windshield.
questions.explanation: Reduce injury risk by wearing an approved helmet, face or eye protection, and protective clothing. A windshield is not essential for injury prevention.

questions.question: When will a helmet NOT provide the best protection?

options.text: If it is free of defects.

questions.correctAnswerText: If it has cracks.
questions.explanation: A helmet must meet DOT and state standards and fit snugly around your head. It must be free of cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps to work properly.

questions.question: What is engine braking?

options.text: It is slowing down by turning the engine off.
It is slowing down by downshifting.
It is not encouraged because it damages the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is slowing down by downshifting.
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear slows your motorcycle, similar to using the brakes. This is called engine braking.
